Risk Statement: An external attacker exploiting password-only authentication on the client VDI gateway, resulting in unauthorised access to EU banking client personal data.
Existing Controls: Password complexity policy; 30-day rotation; account lockout after 5 attempts
Treatment Actions: Deploy phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) on all VDI gateway access; enforce conditional access by device posture; disable legacy authentication protocols

Risk Statement: A departing contractor retaining active client system access after assignment end, resulting in unauthorised access to US banking client source code and audit finding under client right-to-audit.
Existing Controls: Manual offboarding checklist owned by delivery managers; no automated trigger from workforce management system
Treatment Actions: Integrate contractor exit trigger from workforce system to IdP; enforce 4-hour deprovisioning SLA; implement quarterly access recertification for all client-facing repositories

Risk Statement: A security incident affecting client personal data being identified but not reported to CERT-In within the mandated 6-hour window, resulting in regulatory enforcement action against Meridian.
Existing Controls: Incident response plan exists; SOC operates 24x7; no defined CERT-In reporting owner or out-of-hours escalation path
Treatment Actions: Define named CERT-In reporting role with 24x7 on-call rota; embed 6-hour reporting clock into incident playbook; conduct two reporting drills per year; pre-draft submission template

Risk Statement: A subprocessor engaged by the BFS unit processing EU client personal data without a signed Article 28 flow-down agreement, resulting in breach of the client data processing agreement.
Existing Controls: Standard vendor onboarding due diligence questionnaire; legal review of contracts above INR 50 lakh only
Treatment Actions: Mandate Article 28 clause set for all subprocessors touching in-scope personal data regardless of contract value; maintain subprocessor register with client notification workflow; annual subprocessor reassessment

Risk Statement: Client production data extracts being copied to delivery-centre local file shares for troubleshooting, resulting in personal data residing outside approved client-dedicated environments.
Existing Controls: Acceptable use policy prohibits local storage; no technical enforcement or detection
Treatment Actions: Prohibit local extract storage by technical control; provision masked non-production data set for troubleshooting; deploy DLP detection on delivery-centre shares; remove existing extracts and evidence deletion

Risk Statement: A misconfigured storage bucket or over-permissive IAM role in a client-dedicated AWS landing zone exposing banking client data to unauthorised principals, resulting in a reportable data breach.
Existing Controls: Landing zone deployed from a Terraform baseline; manual peer review of infrastructure pull requests; no continuous configuration scanning; no drift detection after deployment
Treatment Actions: Deploy continuous CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark scanning with automated reporting; enable IAM Access Analyzer across all in-scope accounts; enforce service control policies preventing public bucket creation; enable CloudTrail organisation-wide with a delivery check; remediate to a defined baseline and re-scan to evidence closure

Risk Statement: Banking client personal data being sent to a third-party general-purpose AI model API by a delivery team building a document-processing service, without a processor agreement covering that provider or a purpose-limitation control, resulting in an unlawful onward transfer.
Existing Controls: Group AI acceptable use policy published; no technical egress control; no approved-model register; provider selection made at project level
Treatment Actions: Establish an approved-model register with per-model data-handling terms and no-training-on-input commitments; route all model calls through a gateway enforcing egress allow-listing and prompt redaction; require an AI impact assessment before any model touches in-scope personal data; extend the subprocessor register to model providers
DPDP Act 2023: Sec 8(1) purpose limitation / Sec 8(2) processor obligations

Risk Statement: A client-facing conversational assistant delivered by the BFS AI practice being deployed to EU end users without disclosing that they are interacting with an AI system, resulting in the client failing its Article 50 transparency obligation and escalating the failure to Meridian.
Existing Controls: Transparency handled ad hoc at project level; no standard disclosure pattern; no pre-release compliance gate
Treatment Actions: Define a mandatory transparency design pattern (AI disclosure at session start; synthetic content marking) and embed it in the AI delivery checklist; add a pre-release AI compliance gate signed by the AI Practice Lead; record disclosure evidence in the client handover pack
